answers.title: Fixing an IMAP mailbox that stops receiving new mail in a desktop client
answers.body:
When a mailbox suddenly stops receiving new messages in a desktop email client (Outlook, Thunderbird, Apple Mail, etc.) while mail still arrives correctly on other devices or in webmail, the most common cause is that the client's stored password no longer matches the current account password - for example after a routine password reset or a forced security update. Sending mail can keep working for a while even after this happens, because outgoing (SMTP) authentication is sometimes cached separately from incoming (IMAP) authentication, which is why only incoming mail appears broken at first.

To fix this: 1) Open your email account's connection settings in the desktop client. 2) Re-enter the current password for the mailbox exactly as used for webmail login. 3) Save the settings and perform a manual send/receive. 4) If the client still does not prompt for a password or continues to fail silently, remove the account from the client entirely and re-add it from scratch using the current credentials, since some clients cache failed authentication state until the account is re-added.

If re-entering the password does not resolve it, also double check that IMAP access itself is still enabled for the mailbox, since some providers disable IMAP automatically after several repeated authentication failures as a security measure.

answers.title: Setting up a forwarding rule to copy incoming mail to another address
answers.body:
A forwarding rule automatically sends a copy of every incoming message from your mailbox to a second address you choose, which is useful for sharing a mailbox with a colleague or archiving mail externally. This is a deliberate, ongoing copy of everything from that point forward - it does not affect whether mail arrives in the original mailbox at all, and it has nothing to do with troubleshooting missing or delayed messages.

To set one up: 1) Open the mail rules section of your webmail settings. 2) Create a new rule with no conditions (so it applies to every message) or a specific condition if you only want certain mail forwarded. 3) Choose the 'Forward to' action and enter the destination address. 4) Save the rule - it takes effect for new mail arriving from that point on; it will not retroactively forward anything already delivered.

answers.title: Why a new agent sees an empty overview even with the Agent role assigned
answers.body:
This is almost always a missing Group membership, not a Role problem. Every ticket in Zammad belongs to exactly one Group (think of a Group as a queue, mailbox, or department - 'Support', 'Sales', 'Billing', and so on), and an overview only ever shows tickets from Groups the logged-in agent is actually a member of. Having the 'Agent' role just marks someone as agent-type staff in general; it says nothing about which of the many Groups in the system they're allowed into.

Open the Support Group's settings page and check its member list - a freshly created user is very often not added to any Group at all by default, which is exactly why their overviews come back empty no matter how many tickets exist. Add the person there, tick at least 'read' access (add 'create' and 'change' too if they should be able to reply and update tickets), and save. There's no need to touch Roles at all for this - the fix lives entirely on the Group side, and it takes effect the next time the agent's overview refreshes.

answers.title: How Organizations control which tickets customers can see from each other
answers.body:
An Organization groups multiple customer accounts together (for example everyone with an email address at the same company), and it controls visibility on the customer side of the portal, not on the agent side. Depending on how an Organization is configured, its members can either only ever see their own individual tickets, or also see every ticket raised by colleagues in the same Organization - handy for a company where several employees jointly manage one support relationship with you.

This is entirely separate from how agents see tickets internally: an agent's access is decided by Group membership regardless of which Organization the ticket's customer belongs to, and a customer's Organization membership has no effect on any agent's queue. If a customer says they can (or can't) see a colleague's ticket, check the Organization's sharing setting; if an agent can't see a queue's tickets, that's a Group question instead.

answers.title: Requesting a refund for a duplicate or accidental charge
answers.body:
If you were charged more than once for the same order, this is usually caused by a temporary network issue or a page reload during checkout, which can submit the payment request twice even though you only clicked 'Pay' once. Duplicate charges are not intentional and are always eligible for a full refund of the extra amount.

To request a refund for a duplicate charge: 1) Locate the order number and the exact amount and date of both charges on your bank or card statement. 2) Contact support with this information, ideally including a screenshot of the statement. 3) Our billing team will verify that both charges reference the same order and, once confirmed, issue a refund for the duplicate amount back to the original payment method. 4) Refunds are typically visible on your statement within 5-10 business days, depending on your bank's processing time.

If the two charges are for genuinely different orders (different order numbers or different amounts), this is not a duplicate charge and the refund process described here does not apply - please contact support separately for that case.

answers.title: Understanding the layout of your monthly invoice PDF
answers.body:
Your monthly invoice PDF is generated automatically on the first day of each billing cycle and sent to the billing email address on file. The invoice is split into several sections: the header shows your account number and billing period; the itemized table lists every individual order placed during that period along with its order number, date, and amount; a subtotal line sums up all itemized orders; and a final section lists any applicable taxes and the grand total charged to your payment method.

If you need a copy of an older invoice, you can download it at any time from the billing section of your account under 'Invoice history', where every past invoice is archived as a PDF. If any line item on the invoice looks unfamiliar, check the order number against your order history first, since bundled or split shipments sometimes appear as separate line items on the same invoice even though they belong to one order.

answers.title: What to do when your password reset link has expired
answers.body:
Password reset links are only valid for a limited time after they are sent, typically a set number of hours, as a security measure. If you wait too long before clicking the link, it will show an 'expired' message instead of letting you choose a new password - this is expected behavior and does not mean anything is wrong with your account.

If your link has expired, simply go back to the login page and click 'Forgot password' again to request a brand new one; the old, expired link cannot be reactivated or extended. Use the newest email you receive and click its link promptly this time. If you request several reset emails in a row, only the link in the most recently sent email will work - all earlier ones become invalid the moment a new one is requested, not just after their own timeout.

answers.title: Why your two-factor authentication code stops working after a minute
answers.body:
Two-factor authentication codes are intentionally short-lived, usually valid for only about 30 to 60 seconds, to limit the window in which a leaked code could be misused. If you type in a code and it's rejected as invalid or expired, the most common cause is simply that too much time passed between generating the code and submitting it - open your authenticator app again for a fresh one rather than reusing an old screenshot or a code you copied earlier.

Also double-check that the clock on your phone or authenticator device is set to automatic network time; a device clock that has drifted out of sync is a common, less obvious reason codes are rejected even when entered quickly.

answers.title: Auto-replying to the customer the moment a ticket is closed
answers.body:
Set this up as a condition-based rule that watches for the state change itself, rather than anything running on a timer. Create a new rule with the condition 'ticket state changed to closed', and give it a notification action that emails the customer with your resolution message. Because the rule reacts to the change happening on that individual ticket, the customer gets the email within moments of the agent clicking 'closed' - there's no delay, no batching with other tickets, and nothing to wait for at a particular time of day.

One thing to watch for: if your closing message could itself cause another status change (rare, but possible with some automation chains), add a guard so the same ticket doesn't re-trigger the rule and send duplicate emails. Otherwise this is a five-minute setup - condition on the state, action to notify, done. The same mechanism works for any other state change too, not just 'closed' - just swap the condition to whichever state you want to react to.

answers.title: Applying a set of changes to several tickets at once with one click
answers.body:
When an agent needs to apply the same set of changes to a handful of tickets right now - for example setting a state, adding a note, and changing the owner all in one go - a saved shortcut lets them select the tickets and apply everything with a single click, instead of clicking through each field on every ticket individually. This only runs when an agent deliberately chooses to apply it to a specific selection; it never fires on its own in reaction to a ticket changing, and it isn't tied to any schedule either.

To create one: define the exact set of field changes you want applied (state, owner, tags, a note text, and so on), give it a clear name describing what it does, and make it available to the relevant Groups. Agents can then select one or more tickets from an overview and apply it whenever they choose to - the timing and the decision to run it are always manual, which is the key difference from anything that reacts automatically to a condition or runs on a timer.

answers.title: Refunds for annual plans
answers.body:
Refund requests for annual plans are handled by the billing team, not in first level.

1. Check in the customer's account when the plan was renewed. Within 30 days of a renewal, a full refund is possible.
2. After 30 days, offer a pro-rata credit for the remaining months instead of a refund.
3. Add the internal note "Refund requested" with the renewal date, and move the ticket to the group Billing.
4. Tell the customer that the billing team confirms the refund or the credit within two working days.

Monthly plans are never refunded; they can be cancelled at the end of the month.

answers.title: Connecting Slack
answers.body: Zammad sends notifications to a Slack channel through an incoming webhook. Create the webhook in Slack, then add it under Admin > Integrations > Slack and pick the groups and events that are posted.
